summary: Feed s138_double is degraded: NDR port is overloaded by microbursts (13.49 Gbps vs 10 Gbps capacity) and encrypted traffic share (94.2%) exceeds 90% tolerance, reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Microburst aggregation exceeding tool port capacity: peak 13.49 Gbps in 1ms burst is 135% of the 10 Gbps NDR port (2 overloaded intervals). Likely multiple TAP/SPAN feeds aggregated to one tool port without load balancing or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR will drop packets at ingress during bursts, causing missed flows, incomplete session reassembly and missed detections despite needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute aggregated traffic across multiple NDR ports/instances with flow-aware (5-tuple) hashing to keep per-port rate <80% of 10 Gbps and eliminate drops while preserving both directions per flow.

findings.root_cause: 94.2% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs NDR tolerance of 90%. Traffic is predominantly encrypted so NDR has no payload visibility without decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requiring full payload cannot inspect inside encrypted sessions; detection efficacy drops to metadata-only, increasing blind spot for C2, exfiltration and lateral movement inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: Offload selective decryption (or provide keys via centralized decrypt zone) before NDR so it receives cleartext for allowed categories while respecting privacy, bringing encrypted share below 90% threshold.
